articles.title: Framing Natural Light: Five Daylighting Strategies in Cabin Architecture
articles.summary: Cabins offer architects opportunities to experiment playfully with architectural form, materials, landscaping, and spatial configurations . Their compact footprints, relatively simple programs, and close proximity to the natural surroundings allow for unconventional design approaches and the ability to test experiential, architectural ideas. Often constructed as spaces of rest, cabin architecture encourages architects to prioritize the experience of inhabiting a space , exploring how individual design elements contribute to the character and atmosphere of the interior .

articles.title: Ersatzneubau Winkel / Kollektiv.w AG
articles.summary: A House in the Green – Nestled between residential buildings and mature trees stood a small former production hall. Originally, it was to be preserved and extended with a senior-friendly apartment, but structural assessments revealed that this would only be possible with extensive interventions. Due to these challenges and the limited space, a replacement building was planned, with a floor plan based on the former hall.

articles.title: What AI Reveals About Architecture That Was Never Built
articles.summary: Some architectural projects only survive as drawings, competition entries, or models in archives. articles.title: A Garden City in the Caribbean: Planning Belize’s New Capital, Belmopan
articles.summary: Located on the Caribbean coast of Central America, Belize is a small country with an intriguing history. It is bordered by Mexico to the north and Guatemala to the west and south, with the Caribbean Sea along its eastern edge. Known as British Honduras for most of its past, it was formally made into a British colony in 1862, long after its Central American neighbors had won their independence from Spain. As the territory transitioned toward independence, it adopted two symbols of its emerging identity: a new name, Belize , and a new capital , which was built not just to govern the new nation,

articles.title: Khao Phra Tamnak House / SPACE | STORY | STUDIO
articles.summary: Set on the gentle hillside of Khao Phra Tamnak, the house is conceived through a flexible design diagram rather than a predetermined architectural form. The project begins with the conditions of the place and the lives to be accommodated: a gradual change in land level, the family's need for generous and usable flat spaces, the principles of Feng Shui, and the presence of neighboring homes. These factors are not treated as separate constraints. They are brought together in a framework that can be tested, adjusted, and extended.

articles.title: Homes Around Trees / architectureRED
articles.summary: Urban housing in India stands at the intersection of rapid urbanization and a shifting sense of identity. The pressures of land scarcity and market-driven development have transformed housing into a commodity, often prioritizing maximum yield over the fundamental idea of home. In the process, the very essence of housing—as a space that fosters identity, community, and rootedness — is increasingly eroded. The relentless stacking of units, the erasure of open space, and the homogenization of urban environments leave little room for meaningful engagement with nature or with each other.
